---
title: "Reverse vaccinology points to pagP as a universal APEC vaccine candidate"
date: 2025-10-15
description: >
  Published in the Journal of Applied Microbiology, our reverse vaccinology
  and host-pathogen analysis identifies pagP as a potential universal vaccine
  candidate against avian pathogenic E. coli — work also featured in
  MAFES Discovers.
categories: [Publications, Media]
---

Avian pathogenic *E. coli* (APEC) is one of the costliest bacterial diseases
in poultry production. In work published in the *Journal of Applied
Microbiology*, our team used **reverse vaccinology** — pangenome analysis and
in-silico antigen prediction — to identify ***pagP*** as a potential universal
vaccine candidate:

> Jia, L., Ye, X., Arick, M.A., Hsu, C.Y., Evans, J.D., Robinson, K.,
> Adhikari, P., & Zhang, L. (2025). Reverse vaccinology and host-pathogen
> analysis reveal pagP as a potential universal vaccine candidate against
> avian pathogenic *Escherichia coli* in poultry. *Journal of Applied
> Microbiology*, 136(10), lxaf253.
> [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/jambio/lxaf253)

The vaccine-development program behind this work was featured by *MAFES
Discovers* in ["Fowl Play: MSU Scientists Develop Chicken Vaccine to Combat
Bacteria"](https://www.mafes.msstate.edu/discovers/article.php?id=321).
